# Project Overview

**Project:** PhD Orthodontics — Website Redesign, SEO Strategy, and Digital Marketing Optimization.

**Team:** Team 6 — Han Mai, Willy Su, Pei Yun Chuang, Xueying Luo, and Yujia Luo.

The bibliography supports the group's work on the PhD Orthodontics website and digital marketing strategy for San Gabriel and Chino Hills. The sources address how patients search for orthodontic information and how they evaluate the quality of health information online.

## Zhang and Kim (2022)

**Reference**

Zhang, Y., & Kim, Y. (2022). Consumers’ Evaluation of Web-Based Health Information Quality: Meta-analysis. *Journal of Medical Internet Research, 24*(4), e36463. <https://doi.org/10.2196/36463>

**Source:** [Publisher's article page](https://www.jmir.org/2022/4/e36463)

**Attachment:** Full-text PDF attached to the Zotero record.

**Research Note**

This meta-analysis synthesizes 147 studies examining how consumers evaluate the quality of web-based health information. It identifies website navigability, visual aesthetics, and ease of understanding as factors strongly associated with perceived information quality. Our group can use these findings to develop criteria for auditing and redesigning the PhD Orthodontics website. In particular, the study supports prioritizing clear navigation, readable patient information, and a well-organized visual presentation. Because it examines health information broadly, it does not directly establish that these improvements will increase orthodontic consultation bookings.

**Tags**

-   patient trust
-   website design
-   website usability

## Crispino et al. (2023)

**Reference**

Crispino, R., et al. (2023). Orthodontic patients and the information found on the web: a cross-sectional study. *BMC Oral Health, 23*(1), 860. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-023-03609-4>

**Source:** [PubMed record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37957643/)

**Attachment:** Full-text PDF attached to the Zotero record.

**Research Note**

This cross-sectional study examines how orthodontic patients and parents or guardians use online information and perceive its reliability. The researchers analyzed 986 valid questionnaires from four countries and found that 64.6% of respondents searched online for orthodontic information before their visit. Among those who searched online, 81% reported Google as their main platform. Our group can use this source to support patient-focused website content, clear FAQs, and a search strategy for PhD Orthodontics in San Gabriel and Chino Hills. Because the findings are self-reported and cross-sectional, they do not establish that SEO or website changes cause more consultation bookings.

**Tags**

-   Google search
-   patient decision-making
-   patient information
:::

::: callout-note
## Application to the Project

The meta-analysis provides criteria for reviewing the website's usability and presentation. The orthodontic survey helps identify the information patients may seek before a consultation. The group can use both sources to inform website content and design, while evaluating the results of any changes separately.
:::

# Example Zotero Item Screenshot

The following screenshots show a completed Zotero record for *Consumers' Evaluation of Web-Based Health Information Quality: Meta-analysis*. Together, they demonstrate the citation information, attached full-text file, research note, and tags stored in the shared Zotero library.

## Citation Information

The Zotero item includes complete citation metadata, including the article title, authors, journal, publication date, volume, issue, DOI, URL, and contributor information.

![Citation information for a completed Zotero item in the Team 6 shared library.](zotero-example-item-info.png){#fig-zotero-item-info width="95%"}

## Attachment, Note, and Tags

The same Zotero item also includes a full-text PDF attachment, a research note explaining the source's relevance to the project, and three descriptive tags.
